name: King of Tyre
overview: The King of Tyre was a male monarch who ruled during the time of King Zedekiah of Judah, as noted in Jeremiah 27:3. His specific tribal affiliation and additional personal details are not recorded in Scripture. This figure represents the leadership of the city-state of Tyre during a significant period in Judah's history.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of Tyre' directly identifies this person as the ruler of Tyre, with no additional personal name or meaning provided. The designation simply reflects his political authority over the city of Tyre as referenced in Jeremiah 27:3.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for the King of Tyre beyond his role as king during Zedekiah's reign. No further relational details are given in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Tyre is significant as a contemporary ruler during the reign of Judah's King Zedekiah, situating him within the geopolitical context of Jeremiah's prophetic ministry. His mention in Jeremiah 27:3 highlights the interconnectedness of regional powers during a turbulent period in Israel's history. This connection underscores the broader narrative of God's sovereignty over nations and kings.
